govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIDallasInvent: This FBI teletype to the House Select Committee on Assassinations is a Bureau wire. The declassified message is a primary source. The committee probed the JFK and King killings. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FortDetrickBiol: Richard Lebherz’s ‘Deterrent — No. 7’ covers the Fort Detrick biological warfare program. Fort Detrick was the bioweapons hub. The program was secret. Nixon ended it in 1969. The file belongs to the government archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GlanzeWalterD_G: This letter concerning a $60,000 loan and IRS debt — creator unknown — is a financial file. Tax debts haunted many. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the business archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-JonesRonaldCoyD: This item — An Evening at The Science Place with Dr. Ronald C. Jones, Dallas County Medical Society — is a program file. The evening drew a crowd. The file belongs to the cultural archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MartinJohnJrDal: This FBI interview — John Martin, Jr. on filming the motorcade — is a Bureau file. The declassified interview is a primary source. Amateur films captured the killing. The interview may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PatchenJerryD_P: Harold Weisberg’s letter to Jerry Patchen — December 15, 1974 — is a researcher’s note. Weisberg kept up a vast correspondence. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PepperWilliamFD: Harold Weisberg’s memo on William Pepper’s book — September 25, 1995 — is a researcher’s note. Pepper defended James Earl Ray. The memo may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
the-voyages-of-captain-scott-retold-from: Charles Turley retells the epic Antarctic voyages of Captain Robert Falcon Scott — from the Discovery expedition to the tragic race for the South Pole. Drawing on Scott's own journals, he brings the heroism and heartbreak of polar exploration to vivid life. A stirring account of courage at the ends of the earth.
ancient-rome-from-the-earliest-times-dow: Robert F. Pennell's school history carries students from Rome's legendary founding — Romulus and Remus, the seven kings — through republic and empire down to the fall of the Western Empire in 476 A.D. Clear, compact, and well organized for classroom use, it served generations of students. A solid first march through two thousand years of Roman history.
